title: Lochs, Glens & Skye
summary: A week-long loop from Inverness: Loch Ness, three nights on the Isle of Skye, the Road to the Isles by ferry, Glencoe and the Cairngorms.

stages.title: Inverness
stages.why: Close to the airport for an easy first evening.

stages.title: Isle of Skye
stages.why: Central on Skye, so every corner of the island is within an hour.

stages.title: Glencoe & Ben Nevis
stages.why: Between Glencoe and Glen Nevis, with plenty of places to stay.

stages.title: Cairngorms
stages.why: Pine forests and lochs, under an hour from the airport.

days.title: Arrival
days.text: Pick up the car and ease in with Scotland's history, a short drive east of the airport.
days.tip: Culloden visitor centre has set opening hours; the battlefield itself is open all the time.

days.title: Loch Ness to Skye
days.text: Follow the Great Glen along Loch Ness, then west to the most photographed castle in Scotland and over the bridge to Skye.
days.tip: Single-track roads start after Kyle of Lochalsh: use the passing places.

days.title: Trotternish loop
days.text: A full loop of the northern peninsula with Skye's famous rock formations.
days.tip: Start early: the Storr car park fills by mid-morning.

days.title: West Skye
days.text: Crystal pools under the Cuillin, a distillery tour and a white beach most visitors skip.
days.tip: Fairy Pools parking is paid; the path is muddy after rain.

days.title: Road to the Isles
days.text: Ferry from Armadale to Mallaig, then silver beaches and the viaduct from the films on the way to Fort William.
days.tip: Book the Armadale–Mallaig ferry ahead in summer.

days.title: Glencoe
days.text: The most dramatic glen in Scotland, then a short gorge walk to a hidden waterfall in Glen Nevis.
days.tip: The Lost Valley path is rough and crosses a stream: good boots needed.

days.title: Into the Cairngorms
days.text: East through the hills, past a ruined barracks on a mound, to a loch with an island castle.
days.tip: Loch an Eilein has a small paid car park.

days.title: Departure
days.text: A short morning drive back to the airport.

entries.title: Culloden Battlefield
entries.notes: Site of the 1746 battle that ended the Jacobite rising, with a strong visitor centre.

entries.title: Clava Cairns
entries.notes: Bronze Age burial cairns among old beech trees, five minutes from Culloden.
entries.why: Free, quiet and atmospheric, yet most battlefield visitors drive past.

entries.title: Urquhart Castle
entries.notes: Ruined castle on the shore of Loch Ness, the classic Nessie lookout.

entries.title: Eilean Donan Castle
entries.notes: Restored castle on a tidal island where three lochs meet.

entries.title: Old Man of Storr
entries.notes: Rock pinnacle above the coast; about 1.5 hours return on a steep path.

entries.title: Kilt Rock & Mealt Falls
entries.notes: Sea cliff with a waterfall dropping straight into the sea; viewpoint next to the car park.

entries.title: Quiraing
entries.notes: Landslip landscape of cliffs and pinnacles; walk part of the ridge path for the views.

entries.title: Fairy Pools
entries.notes: Clear blue pools and waterfalls below the Black Cuillin, about 40 minutes walk each way.

entries.title: Talisker Distillery
entries.notes: Skye's oldest working distillery; tours are popular, so book ahead.

entries.title: Coral Beach
entries.notes: A bright white beach made of crushed coralline seaweed, a 20-minute walk from the road end.
entries.why: Far from the main loop, so it is often quiet even in summer.

entries.title: Ferry Armadale → Mallaig
entries.notes: About 45 minutes across the Sound of Sleat; car spaces sell out in summer.

entries.title: Silver Sands of Morar
entries.notes: A string of white beaches with views to the islands of Eigg and Rum.
entries.why: One of the finest beaches in the Highlands, on a road most people only drive through.

entries.title: Glenfinnan Viaduct & Monument
entries.notes: The curved railway viaduct known from the Harry Potter films, above Loch Shiel.

entries.title: Glencoe Visitor Centre
entries.notes: Exhibitions, walks and the best overview of the glen's geology and history.

entries.title: Lost Valley (Coire Gabhail) walk
entries.notes: A hidden valley between the Three Sisters, about 3 hours return.

entries.title: Steall Falls gorge walk
entries.notes: A short gorge path to a meadow with one of Scotland's highest waterfalls.
entries.why: Feels remote but starts from a road-end car park near Fort William.

entries.title: Commando Memorial
entries.notes: Memorial with wide views over Ben Nevis and the Great Glen.

entries.title: Ruthven Barracks
entries.notes: Roofless 18th-century barracks on a mound, free to visit.
entries.why: An easy, free stop with real history, rarely busy.

entries.title: Loch an Eilein
entries.notes: Flat loch-side walk through Caledonian pine forest to a castle on an island.

extras.season: May is one of the driest months in the Highlands, with long days and fewer midges than July and August.

bookBy.what: Accommodation on Skye: it fills up first.
Check the weather for the hill walks and pack midge repellent.

documents: Car hire booking and credit card

budget.includes: Accommodation, food, fuel, entry fees and the ferry, per person per day.
budget.notes: Skye is the most expensive part.

notes.text: Many Highland roads are single track. Pull into passing places to let others pass, and never park in them.
Distances look short, but averages are slow on narrow roads: plan for about 50 km/h.
